title: Blood Magic
description: Quests for the Blood Magic progression path.

quests.title: Bloodmagic Qualification
description: To begin Blood Magic research, you need to get the required gamestage which can be obtained from the Malum questline

quests.title: Soul Hunter
description: Will does not fall out of mobs on its own - snare one first, then kill it while it is tangled.
Until the aura machines exist this is your only tap for Demonic Will, so make snares in bulk.

quests.title: Soul Stealer
description: Demonic Will is Blood Magic's second currency - the Hellfire Forge burns it instead of LP.
Nothing in this chapter moves until you hold one. Even the altar asks for Will before it will assemble.

quests.title: Tinkering With Soul
description: The Forge is the mod's other workshop, and it runs on Will rather than LP - so it works long before your altar is worth anything.
Every Tartaric Gem and every soul-forged alloy in this chapter comes out of it.

quests.title: Soul Stone
description: A Tartaric Gem banks Demonic Will instead of leaving you to carry it loose. Petty is the entry rung; each gem above it is the price of admission to something that wants Will in bulk.

quests.title: More Souls
description: A bigger bank, and a gate in its own right - the Forge will not sell you the better recipes while you are still holding the smallest gem.

quests.title: Soul Reaper
description: Common is the gem the aura machines demand. The Crucible and the Crystallizer refuse anything smaller, so the Will economy stalls here until you climb this rung.

quests.title: Beyond Soul
description: The top of the gem ladder, priced in Demon Realm goods. Will collection ends where the dungeon rituals begin.

quests.title: Alchemy Table
description: The alchemist's bench. Reagents no crafting grid will produce - ashes, powders, the flask line - all start here.
Sanguine Scientiem has the catalogue; the table itself has the rest.

quests.title: Why Not Use Chalk
description: Ashes let you draw an Alchemy Array: a craft performed on the ground rather than in a grid. The early sigils exist nowhere else.

quests.title: See the Soul
description: Reads the LP standing in an altar and the Will hanging in the air around you. Without it you are guessing at both numbers for the rest of the chapter.

quests.title: Blood Altar
description: The heart of Blood Magic - nearly everything else in the mod is transmuted inside it.

A bare basin is Tier 1. Every tier above that is bought with rings of Blood Runes, and each tier unlocks a fixed set of recipes rather than a gradual improvement. Sanguine Scientiem lists which tier buys what.

quests.title: Mystic Stone Tablet
description: Slates are the backbone of every recipe in this chapter, and the blank one is most of what a Tier 1 altar is for. Expect a harder slate waiting at every tier above it.

quests.title: Weak Blood Orb
description: Bind an orb and every altar you own feeds one shared Soul Network - the pool that pays for sigils, rites and runes.
Blood Runes are built around this orb, so Tier 1 hands you the key to every tier above it.

quests.title: Tier 2: The First Ring
description: The first ring of runes pays out four ways at once: Reinforced Slate, the Apprentice Orb, the Alchemy Flask, and the Dagger of Sacrifice that finally lets something other than you bleed.
Runes laid at this tier are mostly structural - hold your upgrade runes until Tier 3, where all of them go live.

quests.title: Tier 3: Pillars and Light
description: Tier 3 turns the altar into a real engine: Imbued Slate, the Magician's Orb and all four elemental Inscription Tools land together. They are siblings, not a chain - take them in any order.
From here on every rune around the basin counts as an upgrade slot, including the ones that were doing nothing before.

quests.title: Tier 4: Crowned in Bloodstone
description: The great unlock - Demonic Slate, the Master Orb, the Dusk Inscription Tool and both Teleposition Foci.
The altar cannot grow past Tier 3 until you have been down into the Demon Realm and dragged something back.

quests.title: Tier 5: The Hellforged Crown
description: The ceiling. Hellforged metal crowns it, smelted from material that exists only inside the demon dungeons, and it buys Ethereal Slate and the Archmage's Orb.
The code hints at a Tier 6; the blocks its corners want were never registered in this pack, so do not go hunting for them.

quests.title: Better Stone Tablet
description: Tier 2's slate - one of the four things that first ring of runes buys you, not a rung you have to climb before the others.

quests.title: Deluxe Stone Tablet
description: Tier 3's slate, arriving alongside the Magician's Orb and the Inscription Tools. One tier, three unlocks.

quests.title: Demonic Slate
description: How many slates are there?? This one waits on Tier 4, in the same payout as the Master Orb and the Teleposition Foci.

quests.title: Gilded Stone Tablet
description: I assure you this is the last slate. Tier 5 unlocks exactly two things - this and the Archmage's Orb - and there is no buildable tier above it.

quests.title: Apprentice Blood Orb
description: Each orb tier raises the ceiling on your Soul Network and opens the recipes that refuse anything weaker.
This one shares a ring of runes with the Reinforced Slate, so build either first.

quests.title: Magician's Blood Orb
description: Every Alchemical Reaction Chamber and every Master Ritual Stone wants this orb in its recipe. Most of the mid-game is waiting on one craft.

quests.title: Master Blood Orb
description: Tier 4's orb, and the wall most players hit.
The Weak Blood Shard it demands stopped being a mob drop in 1.20 - it is grown now, not killed for - which is why the Demon Realm gates this one.

quests.title: Archmage's Blood Orb
description: The last rung of the Soul Network ladder. Nothing in the tail of this chapter will accept a lesser orb, so the endgame starts the moment this one binds.

quests.title: Alchemical Reaction Chamber
description: 1.20 Blood Magic's workhorse. What comes out of it depends on the catalyst left sitting inside, and it runs without any Soul Network link at all.
It is also this pack's ore multiplier once you have worked the chain out, which is most of what makes the rest of this chapter affordable.
Sanguine Scientiem covers the catalysts. The Reverter and the Hydration Cell are the two that unblock the Master Blood Orb, so start there.

quests.title: Blood From Fruit
description: Shards are not a mob drop any more. They are pulled out of Demon Realm fruit in the reaction chamber, which is why the dungeon comes first.
Carry fruit home and plant it - Tau is a crop once you own a single one, so the trip below is a one-time toll.
Bloodstone, the Master Orb and the last Tartaric Gem are all paid for in fruit from here on.

quests.title: Elemental Inscription
description: Four tools, one per element, that paint blank Ritual Stones into the stones a rite actually calls for. They never wear out.
The Ritual Diviner swallows all four whole, which is the only reason you need a complete set.

quests.title: Heart of the Rite
description: A ritual is a pattern of inscribed stones laid around one master stone, and the master is the only block you ever click.
By hand that means placing dozens of stones exactly right; the Diviner places them for you. It is the difference between rituals being a curiosity and being infrastructure.

A finished pattern sits inert until an activation crystal pays for it out of your Soul Network. Every rite in this pack accepts the weak crystal - the awakened one is not obtainable here and is never needed.

quests.title: Edge of the Hidden Realm
description: Nothing in this pack generates a Blood Magic dungeon in the world. This rite carves one, under a pillar it raises on the spot.

Its vaults are the only source of Tau Fruit, Demon Will Crystals, and the Demonite and Hellforged Sand the top two altar tiers are built from - everything the rest of this chapter is short of is down there.
A deeper rite, Pathway to the Endless Realm, opens a far larger version of the same place for a far larger price.

quests.title: Well of Suffering
description: The rite that ends bloodletting: everything that dies in its zone pipes its life essence straight into a linked altar.

It calls for Dusk stones, and the plain Diviner cannot draw those - upgrade the Diviner before you plan the build. Afterwards the Ritual Tinkerer will move the damage zone if your mob source does not sit where the rite put it.

tasks.text: I have laid and lit the Well of Suffering

quests.title: Aura Made Solid
description: Will inside a gem is only useful to you. The Crucible bleeds it out into the chunk as an aura, and rituals and will-hungry machines drink from that aura instead of your pocket.
Stand a Crystallizer in a saturated aura and it grows a crystal cluster on its own lid - the longer you leave it before harvesting, the more it drops.
Between the two you stop hunting Will and start farming it.

quests.title: Blood Sacrifice
description: Your own health is the first LP supply, and the knife is how you spend it. Crude, slow and genuinely dangerous - most of what follows in this chapter exists to get you off it.

quests.title: Blood Infused Wood
description: Blood Arsenal branches off here. Its whole tree of gear grows out of wood the altar has soaked.

quests.title: Forged With Blood
description: Handle stock for Blood Arsenal. A small step, but nothing further up that branch is built without a stack of these.

quests.title: Telepathy
description: Will pressed into metal - the first thing the Hellfire Forge makes that is not a gem, and a tool material in its own right. The Smithery book has its stats.

quests.title: Soul Bound
description: What the altar makes of good steel, and the gate on this whole chapter: claiming it marks you a skilled wizard, which is what the rest of the pack has been waiting on.

quests.title: Stage recovery
description: Gamestages is a bit weird sometimes! If the stage from "Soul Bound" did not stick, claim this to get it back.
Safe to use more than once.

quests.title: Warp Engine
description: A focus is a bound location and nothing more. Tier 4 sells you the first one; what it points at only matters once you own the block that reads it.

quests.title: Hyperspace Engine
description: More reach. The plain focus barely leaves the room - this is the one that makes teleposition worth wiring into a base.

quests.title: The Teleposer
description: A focus on its own only records a pair of coordinates. The Teleposer is the block that performs the swap, exchanging everything inside its own cube with the volume the bound focus points at - blocks, items, mobs and you.
Two of them and one focus make a permanent two-way freight link, which is why this quest wants a pair.

quests.title: Dance of Life
description: The top of Blood Arsenal, priced like it: an endgame altar, an endgame orb, and a great deal of LP burnt in one go. Everything that mod makes worth carrying wants one.

quests.title: Overbled
description: The pack's own alloy and the last thing Blood Magic gives you. It binds in the Hellfire Forge rather than the altar, and every branch of this chapter - gems, slates, rituals, arsenal - has to be finished before it will.
